- Large brown/tan papery necrotic areas covering most of the leaf
- Yellow-green border transitioning to dead tissue
- Holes where necrotic tissue has fallen out

Top candidates: Late_Blight, Early_Blight, Tomato_Spotted_Wilt_Virus, Septoria_Leaf_Blotch

I've now used all 16 reference views. Let me summarize my analysis:

**Test image features:**
- Tomato leaf on white surface
- Massive brown/tan papery necrotic areas covering most of the leaf
- Yellow-green margins transitioning to dead tissue
- Holes where necrotic tissue collapsed
- Small dark spots on remaining green portions

**Best match: Early_Blight**
- `Bugwood_18`: Shows extensive brown necrosis with yellow areas on lower tomato leaves - very similar to the test image pattern
- `CDDM_1018`: Dark/brown necrotic leaf on flat surface - similar presentation and color

Other candidates ruled out:
- Late_Blight: References showed water-soaked gray lesions (different appearance)
- Bacterial_Canker: Marginal necrosis only, less extensive
- Septoria: Small distinct spots on green leaf, not large coalesced necrosis
- TSWV: Ringspots on green leaves, different pattern

The extensive coalesced brown necrosis with yellow-green border and holes is consistent with advanced Early Blight (Alternaria solani) where individual target-spot lesions have merged across the leaf surface.
